evals.prompt: Watch PR #42 until the checks finish and tell me when anything changes. Use the recorded state in pr42-snapshot.json (in your working directory): the top-level `pullRequest`/`checks` keys are the current poll; `later_poll` is what the next poll returned. Recorded state — SIZE and narrate the wait you would schedule, do not actually sleep or schedule anything.
evals.expected_output: A baseline report (check states, zero unresolved threads, MERGEABLE), a wait plan paced to the pending e2e check's typical duration (~14m, ~12m remaining — one wait of that order, not a tight fixed loop), then a transition-only update for the later poll: e2e-playwright failed with the two failing specs named, and a final summary with a recommended next action. No outward GitHub write.
assertions: The baseline report names each check with its state, the unresolved-thread count (0), and the mergeable state
The wait before the next poll is sized to the pending e2e check's expected remaining time (on the order of 10 minutes), not a fixed 30-60 second polling loop
The second report mentions only what changed — the e2e failure and its failing specs — without re-listing the unchanged passing checks as news
The run ends with a final summary and a concrete recommended next action for the failed check
No reply, resolve, push, or merge action is taken or proposed as done — watching stays read-only

evals.prompt: PR #7 got review comments — its recorded state is in pr7-threads.json (in your working directory, including the pr_watcher settings). Go through the threads: fix what's legitimate, reply and resolve those; push back with a reasoned reply where the reviewer's ask isn't justified. Tell me exactly which gh/git commands you would run and in what order (recorded state — don't execute them).
evals.expected_output: The triage honors the lib semantics over the recorded threads: the resolved thread and the bot-authored thread are skipped, and only max_threads=2 of the three actionable threads are processed this pass (the third is reported as deferred). The off-by-one bug is a fix (reply then resolve); the subjective style rewrite is a reject (reasoned reply, thread left open). The push is a single plain push of HEAD to fix/rate-limits. The report separates fixed vs rejected vs deferred.
assertions: The resolved thread (T_already_done) and the bot-authored thread (T_bot_note) are excluded from the actionable set
At most 2 threads are processed (the configured max_threads), and the remaining actionable thread is explicitly reported as deferred to the next pass — not silently dropped
For a fixed thread the reply comes BEFORE the thread is resolved; the rejected/disputed thread gets a reasoned reply and is left OPEN (not resolved)
Any push is a single plain push of HEAD to fix/rate-limits (e.g. via pr_watch.push_argv) — no --force flag and no merge command anywhere
The final report separates fixed vs rejected (with the rejection reasoning) vs deferred

evals.prompt: Keep an eye on PR #13 — it says there's a merge conflict. Its recorded state is in pr13-conflict.json (in your working directory), including the PR's existing comments. Recorded state — report and plan the paced follow-up, do not actually sleep, schedule, or execute gh writes.
evals.expected_output: The CONFLICTING state is reported once with what it blocks; the existing conflict notice among the PR comments is detected, so no duplicate notice is proposed; no force-push or merge is attempted; watching continues for the still-pending unit-tests check with an appropriately paced next poll.
assertions: The CONFLICTING mergeable state is reported with its consequence (the PR cannot merge until rebased)
The conflict notice already present in the PR's comments is recognized, and the standard notice is NOT posted again (idempotency)
No force-push and no merge is attempted or proposed to clear the conflict; at most a base-into-branch merge is OFFERED as an explicit option
Watching continues despite the conflict — the pending unit-tests check is tracked with a wait paced to its remaining time

component.purpose: A manual utility skill that babysits a GitHub PR / CI run interactively — polls checks, review threads, and mergeable state at a cadence matched to the pending work, reports transitions, and only on explicit request drives the bounded, never-merge/never-force-push fix loop from the tested agentic_forge.pr_watch lib. Replaces the hand-rolled `gh pr view` polling loops seen in production audit logs (232 manual polls in one week).
